clue.text: Artful application of geometry

parts.note: an art movement whose painters built pictures out of cubes, cones and flat geometric planes

explanation.surface: A clever use of shapes and angles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picasso and Braque school of painting broke subjects into geometric solids, applying geometry to art.

clue.text: Technical term for what the hungry dog might do

definitions.text: Technical term for what the hungry dog might do

parts.words: Technical term for what the hungry dog might do
parts.note: a hungry dog might collar a bone, that is grab one; collarbone is the everyday name of this bone

explanation.surface: Asking for the proper word for a hungry dog's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: To collar is to seize, so a dog might 'collar bone'; the anatomist's name for the collarbone is the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical name for the collarbone, punned as a hungry dog seizing a bone.

clue.text: Now-every maze of quick (Tennyson)

parts.note: Tennyson's In Memoriam has 'Now ... every maze of quick', the hedges coming into leaf; fill the gap

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from Tennyson's poem of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' is quickset, a hawthorn hedge, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's verb means sprouts or buds, the hedges putting out new growth in spring.

clue.text: The little limbs could cause a dangerous fire

definitions.meaning: short arms, literally small upper limbs
pistols and rifles carried by hand give hand-weapon fire

explanation.surface: Tiny limbs might start a hazardous blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' suggests flames; it is gunfire from hand-held weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand guns and rifles are the portable weapons, and literally the phrase means short limbs.

clue.text: Five hundred in Capri develop a metric system

indicators.note: to develop is to work something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: Building in Capri brings in a new system of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' shuffles D, IN and CAPRI together. 'metric' here is about verse metre, not measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pindaric verse follows the irregular metre of the Greek poet Pindar's odes, a scheme of poetic metre.

clue.text: A topping sweet, but unpopular with airlines

definitions.meaning: sugar frosting spread on top of a cake
ice forming on aircraft wings is a flying hazard

explanation.surface: A delicious dessert that air carriers dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' reads as old slang for excellent, but it is literal: frosting tops a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Cake frosting is a sweet topping, and frozen build-up on wings is a danger to aircraft.

clue.text: They are distributed by American dealers

definitions.text: They are distributed by American dealers

parts.words: They are distributed by American dealers
parts.note: in American usage a pack of playing cards is called by another name, and card dealers deal them out

explanation.surface: Goods handed out by American traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealers' suggests merchants; they are card dealers, and Americans say decks for packs of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call packs of playing cards by this word, and dealers hand them out.

clue.text: Show a lever

annotationWithheld.why: Show a lever (6): REVEAL is an anagram of 'a lever' with 'Show' the definition, but no clue word signals the anagram

clue.text: In the theatre this might be dangerous

definitions.text: In the theatre this might be dangerous

parts.words: In the theatre this might be dangerous
parts.note: the theatre is a theatre of war, where gunpowder granulated into grains is hazardous; it also suggests corny, trite acting

explanation.surface: A warning about a hazard on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage; read it as a theatre of war, where granulated gunpowder is explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder formed into grains is the corned kind, dangerous stuff in a war zone.

clue.text: Will this make the reception a success? Not an earthly

definitions.text: Will this make the reception a success?
definitions.meaning: a rooftop antenna is what gives good television or radio reception
something in or of the air is not of the earth

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a party will go well, and fearing it has no chance at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not an earthly' is British slang for 'no chance at all', which hides the literal sense of belonging to the air rather than the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV antenna secures good reception, and the adjective means of the air, the opposite of earthly.

clue.text: Find out that the record has finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
something that has finished is over

explanation.surface: Learning that the music has stopped playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out a fact is to come upon it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: It's the highway to one of the stars

definitions.text: It's the highway to one of the stars

parts.words: It's the highway to one of the stars
parts.note: each US state is a star on the American flag, and a famous wartime highway leads to the northernmost state

explanation.surface: A road said to lead to celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests fame or the sky; each star on the US flag is a state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alaska Highway runs from Canada to the state of that name, one of the flag's fifty stars.

clue.text: I'm in the market for what's not really obtainable

parts.note: the speaker, I, as the subject of the trading
someone in the market buys and sells, that is, they deal

explanation.surface: A shopper says they are looking to buy something that cannot really be had.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm in the market' as 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect standard is something aimed at but never quite reached in practice.

clue.text: Supporter I scold, having to lay down the law

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
to slate someone is to criticise them harshly

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a helper while being bossy.
explanation.definitionFit: To make laws is literally to lay down the law, an idiom for enacting rules.

clue.text: Main craft of the make-up artist

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, and a big passenger ship crosses it
eyeliner, a cosmetic pencil, is part of a make-up artist's kit

explanation.surface: The chief skill of someone who does stage make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief', but in crosswords the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean steamer is a vessel on the high seas, and eyeliner is a cosmetic the make-up artist uses.

clue.text: It's unnecessary to behave so officiously to postpone a dissolution

definitions.text: It's unnecessary to behave so officiously to postpone a dissolution

parts.words: It's unnecessary to behave so officiously to postpone a dissolution
parts.note: a paraphrase of Clough's lines 'Thou shalt not kill; but need'st not ... officiously to keep alive', the missing verb being the entry

explanation.surface: A remark that there is no need to be busybodyish in delaying a breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Hugh Clough's poem The Latest Decalogue says one need not try hard officiously to keep a dying person alive; 'postpone a dissolution' is 'keep alive'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted verb means to make great efforts, the action Clough says is unnecessary.

clue.text: A stern director, of course

parts.note: a stern is the back of a ship, and the blade fitted there steers the vessel's course

explanation.surface: A strict manager, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stern director' suggests a strict boss and 'of course' an aside; read 'stern' as the back of a ship and 'course' as its heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's steering blade at the stern directs the vessel's course.

clue.text: Composer and painter give the copper a deposit

definitions.note: the definition describes the green deposit on copper, a noun

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer
Juan Gris was a Spanish Cubist painter

explanation.surface: An opera writer and an artist pay the police officer some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the copper' looks like slang for a police officer, as if being bribed; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The green crust that forms on weathered copper and bronze is a deposit on the metal.

clue.text: Pelt the Pawnee! That's a painful thing

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's fur
read as 'pawn-ee', the one who receives pawned goods; the pawnbroker is called 'uncle' in old slang

explanation.surface: An order to throw things at a Native American, with a painful result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb and 'Pawnee' a Native American people; one who takes pledges is the pawnbroker, known as 'uncle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil is an inflamed, sore swelling of the skin, a painful thing.

clue.text: Like the Needles, for those wishing to tack?

definitions.text: Like the Needles, for those wishing to tack?

parts.words: Like the Needles, for those wishing to tack?
parts.note: sewing needles get a strand passed through their eyes before tacking stitches; the Needles also suggests the rocks off the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: Sailors tacking past the Needles rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, and to tack is to sail zigzag; here it means loose sewing stitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles with thread run through their eyes are ready for tacking, the loose sewing stitch.

clue.text: " No man is an -" (Donne)

parts.note: John Donne's Meditation XVII begins 'No man is an ... entire of itself'; fill the gap

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from John Donne's famous meditation.
explanation.definitionFit: Donne's line compares a person to a piece of land surrounded by water, which no man is.

clue.text: Justice for the hooligan?

parts.note: the word goes before 'justice' for summary punishment, and as a noun it means a thug

explanation.surface: Asking what punishment a thug should get.
explanation.walkthrough: Rough justice is harsh, summary punishment, and a rough is a violent lout, so the word does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy thug is a 'rough', and harsh summary punishment is 'rough justice'.

clue.text: What the naughty child did causes a collision

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
what someone did is a deed, an act

explanation.surface: A misbehaving youngster's antics lead to a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'What the naughty child did' as 'imp act'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful striking of one thing against another is a collision.

clue.text: Put in an appearance at ten dinners

annotationWithheld.why: Put in an appearance at ten dinners (6): ATTEND is hidden in 'at ten dinners', but the only possible signal word 'in' belongs to the definition 'Put in an appearance', so it would do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Put in an appearance at ten dinners

clue.text: The French underground had little spirit, maybe, for marking time

parts.note: the Metro is the Paris underground railway

indicators.note: maybe here admits the spelling is only roughly matched, signalling the word should be judged by sound

parts.note: a gnome is a small earth spirit of folklore

explanation.surface: The Paris subway once had a small ghost, keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' admits the little spirit's word is only matched by ear, since its first letter is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician's ticking device beats out a steady tempo, so it is for marking time.

clue.text: Start chipping here, if you like, with a tortured groan

definitions.text: Start chipping here, if you like

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer begins chipping, groaning in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: Chipping Ongar is a small town in Essex, England: after 'Chipping' you start this word if you like.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essex town is Chipping Ongar, so it is the place name that follows 'Chipping'.

clue.text: Saxon royalty seen at Ciro's ?

annotationWithheld.why: Saxon royalty seen at Ciro's? (5): OSRIC is an anagram of 'Ciro's', but no clue word signals the anagram

clue.text: Accustom to the union, that's about it

indicators.note: that's is read as 'that has', so the word for about holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: in re is Latin legal shorthand for 'in the matter of', meaning about
U is a standard abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: Getting used to the trade union, and that's all there is to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's about it' reads as 'that (IN RE) has it (U)'.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden someone to hardship is to make them used to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Engraves a popular series

annotationWithheld.why: Engraves a popular series (8): AVENGERS is an anagram of 'Engraves', but no clue word signals the anagram

clue.text: Ready for straining

parts.note: a person steadied for a strain is prepared, and a structure fitted with struts is made to take strain

explanation.surface: Prepared to strain something through a sieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straining' suggests a sieve in the kitchen; it means bearing a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone steeled for a shock is prepared, and a wall propped with struts can take strain.

clue.text: On the main speedway it sounds like a dead-heat

indicators.note: these words say the entry is a word heard the same as another phrase

parts.note: a dead heat is a contest where the leaders tie, a tied race

explanation.surface: Racing on the main track, where the finish was a dead heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea: a strong fast current at sea is a speedway on the main.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift tidal current runs through a narrow sea channel, a fast track on the ocean.

clue.text: Go back up the family tree!

definitions.text: Go back up the family tree!

parts.words: Go back up the family tree!
parts.note: to climb is to go up, and one's forebears are the people further up a family line

explanation.surface: An instruction to trace one's ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' suggests going into the past on the tree; the word simply means climb, and also echoes the old word for forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to go up, and climbing a family tree takes you towards your forebears.
